sources.name: Gourmet Gift Baskets most-searched fruits in the US (Google Keyword Planner), via Delish/Yahoo

sources.name: The Harris Poll for Instacart, summer stone fruit (n=2,090 US adults, May 2024)
sources.method: Stone fruit Americans most look forward to this summer: Peaches 62%, Cherries 49%, Mangoes 40%, Plums 35%, Nectarines 30%. Covers stone fruit only, so it was used just to order peaches, cherries, mango, plums and nectarines, not in the average.

changes_vs_current: Lemons #5 -> #15: their high spot came from purchase and consumption data, which count lemons bought as an ingredient. On liking, YouGov has them #9 at 79%, tied with blueberries and tangerines. They miss the search top 8 and are behind every gut-check fruit, so they sit just below the 11.75-12.6 average cluster.
Limes #15 -> #19: the same ingredient effect. YouGov has them #13 (72%), they miss the search top 8, and they rank #16 on Packer purchases and #12 on USDA.
Apples #6 -> #5: #2 on USDA fresh consumption, top-4 on Packer purchases, tied #1 for liked taste in the watermelon board survey, and a top-3 gut answer.
Oranges #9 -> #6: averages 5.0 across the 4 sources that measured them (Packer #6, USDA #6, search #3, liked taste #5) and is a top gut answer. YouGov has no entry for oranges.
Pineapple #8 -> #7: YouGov #5 (83%). Purchase and USDA ranks #11 and #7.
Blueberries #7 -> #8: in all 5 sources but mid-pack in each (YouGov #7, Packer #7, USDA #15, search #8, liked taste 64%).
Peaches #13 -> #9: averages 9.5 across 4 sources (Packer #9, search #6, liked taste 69%, USDA #16) and is #1 in the Harris stone-fruit poll at 62%. A gut-check answer.

Cherries #17 -> #10: averages 12.3 across 3 sources. Moved up as a gut-check answer and because the Harris stone-fruit poll puts it above mango (49% vs 40%), with search #7 and Packer #12. No source puts it near #17 except USDA tonnage (#18).
Mango #14 -> #11: averages 12.25 across 4 sources. #1 in search and a gut answer, but YouGov #16 (71%) and Packer #19 keep it out of the top 10.
Avocado #16 -> #12: averages 11.75 (USDA #5, Packer #10, YouGov #19 at 69%). Kept below the gut-check fruits because it is mostly bought as an ingredient.
Clementines #10 -> #13: YouGov tangerines #8 (79%), but Packer #18. The average of 12.0 puts it in the 11-16 cluster.
Cantaloupe #19 -> #14: averages 11.8 across 4 sources (USDA #10, Packer #13, YouGov #14). Kept below gut-check fruits because only 58% say they like the taste.
Blackberries #12 -> #16: YouGov #6 (80%), but only 2 sources cover it (Packer #17), so the average is 12.0.
Raspberries #11 -> #17: averages 14.75 (YouGov #11, Packer #14, USDA #21).
Pears #20 -> #18: a gut-check answer, but Packer #15 and USDA #14 keep it out of the top 12.
Pomegranate #23 -> #20: search #5, but YouGov #22 (63%).
Honeydew added at #21: averages 17.4 across 3 sources (YouGov 67%, USDA #19, liked taste 48%).
Nectarines #21 -> #22, Kiwi #22 -> #23, Plums #18 -> #24: tail fruits with averages from 17.75 to 18.5. Plums rank #18-#23 everywhere.
Grapefruit #24 -> dropped: now has data, and it ranks low (YouGov #24 of 26 at 60%, USDA #17, average 19.75). Honeydew, Nectarines, Kiwi and Plums all average higher.
Unchanged: Bananas #1, Strawberries #2, Grapes #3, Watermelon #4.
confidence: medium: the top 8 agree across 5 independent US people sources, but no open-ended 'name your favorite fruit' US poll could be found, so positions 9-18 rest on liking, purchase, consumption and search data that fall in a tight cluster.
